claim: Attributes already on T are ignored, which breaks an acceptance criterion. With no SurrogateType, the collector always calls CreateContractlessMembers(type), which takes every public read-write member. It never checks T for [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] or [DataContract]/[DataMember]/[IgnoreDataMember]. A member marked [IgnoreMember], or left out of a [DataContract], is still serialized. Keys are also member names instead of the declared Key/Order values, so the wire format differs from the dynamic resolver for the same type.

claim: Contractless mode here differs from the library's existing contractless behaviour. Get-only public properties are silently dropped, because IsPublicReadWrite requires a public setter. Classes without an accessible parameterless constructor are rejected with MsgPack007, because constructorParameters is always empty. DynamicContractlessObjectResolver serializes readable public members and matches constructor parameters. Immutable library types, which are typical of a zero-dependency NuGet library, therefore get either an incomplete formatter or none.

claim: When the formatted type T has MessagePack or DataContract attributes, the generator ignores them. The requirement says these attributes must be honoured. With no surrogate, `CreateContractlessMembers` runs unconditionally and never reads T's attributes. As a result, `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key(n)]`, `[IgnoreMember]`, `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]` and `[IgnoreDataMember]` on T have no effect. Every public read-write member is serialized under its name as a string key, including members marked `[IgnoreMember]`. Integer keys declared with `[Key(0)]` become string-keyed maps, so the wire format does not match T's declared contract.

claim: The 'exactly one data type' rule that MsgPack020 states is not enforced. The guard only checks `formatterInterfaces.Length == 0`. claim: The contractless member key order is alphabetical by name (OrderBy Ordinal). The existing contractless behaviour in MessagePack, ContractlessStandardResolver, uses declaration or reflection order for maps. Bytes produced by the generated formatter therefore differ in key order from the dynamic contractless resolver for the same type. Deserialization is key-based so it still works, but byte equality and interop with existing contractless payloads is not preserved.
